summary.headline: IDFC First Q4 FY26 reported PAT of Rs 319 crore after a Rs 646 crore fraud charge; management puts normalised PAT at Rs 746 crore.
summary.overview: Reported Q4 PAT of Rs 319 crore absorbed an upfront fraud impact (Rs 480 crore post-tax on Rs 646 crore principal claims), a Rs 159 crore pre-tax treasury loss and a Rs 173 crore tax refund gain. Management's normalised PAT is Rs 746 crore, up about 145% YoY, and FY26 PAT adjusted for the fraud was Rs 2,119 crore (up 39%). Loans grew 20% YoY to about Rs 2.9 lakh crore, but customer deposits grew only 1% QoQ, which management attributes to SA rate cuts, the fraud incident, tight liquidity and the West Asia crisis. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 1.61% and credit cost at 1.63% in Q4 versus 2.13% for FY26. Management guided FY27 NIM at about 5.75%, opex growth of 13-14%, and credit cost of 170-180 bps, but would not commit to a 1% ROA timeline.

segments.name: Retail, rural and MSME
segments.commentary: Gross NPA improved 8 bps to 1.47% and net NPA improved 7 bps to 0.56%. Gross slippages fell about 15% QoQ and net slippages about 27% QoQ. SMA 1+2 improved from 0.88% to 0.78%.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book about Rs 6,662 crore, with 89% covered under CGFMU. Disbursements rose about 27% QoQ, collection efficiency improved from 99.4% to 99.7%, and slippages fell to Rs 96 crore from Rs 153 crore. SMA fell 70 bps to 0.79%. Management expects the book to grow 15-20% in FY27.

segments.name: Wholesale and corporate
segments.commentary: Management said the corporate book was reduced from about Rs 68,000 crore to about Rs 36,000 crore through de-growth of project and infrastructure loans, and that it is now growing again.

segments.name: Wealth management
segments.commentary: AUM grew about 23% YoY to about Rs 57,000 crore.

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Crossed 4.5 million cards in the quarter, with the book growing about 22% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 NIM expected to stay broadly around FY26's 5.75%; management declined to guide a Q4-level margin as the run-rate.
FY27 opex growth guided at 13-14%, with Q1 FY27 likely higher than that range and the rate coming down over Q2-Q4.
FY27 top-line growth expected at about 18-18.5%, with MFI contributing positively again.
FY27 credit cost expected at 170-180 bps (FY26: 213 bps), including some benefit from CGFMU cover.
Management expects Q1 FY27 deposit growth to be strong and loan growth to be around 5% QoQ; no explicit ROA target given beyond 'kissing distance' of 1%.
Further deposit rate cuts are unlikely, but a move of up to 10 bps upward is possible depending on market conditions. The SA rate was changed on 21 April, with an impact of only a few bps.
capex_capacity: About 80 branches were shut in Q4 FY26, and Q1 FY27 opex will carry increment costs.
Liability-side drag fell to about 1.0% from 1.2% last year, and management expects it to continue declining.
Management expects capital to need a reset, and ECL transition capital could be needed once final RBI guidelines are issued; the timing is still unclear.
Average LCR is maintained at 114-115%, which management considers comfortable.
Contingency provision on MFI: Rs 130 crore carried forward into FY27 after Rs 35 crore used in Q4.
demand_pricing: Cost of funds fell to about 6% in Q4, down over 50 bps in one year. Management said it dropped the SA rate from 7% to 6.5%.
Loss of high-ticket, high-rate deposits after the incident; management said the broader base did not leave.
Management said April has started well, with new account openings in March as strong as February.
Management said yield on the book is 13%+ and credit cost about 2%, and that the lending business ROA should be about 1.5-1.6% of loans in FY27.
Liability side ROA drag remains; management says the bank's liability cost-income ratio of about 145% should trend towards 100 over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the monthly deposit accretion and when will growth return to normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects Q1 FY27 to show strong growth and a return to about 5% QoQ deposit growth, citing strong March and April account openings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 treasury loss linked to the equity stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a Rs 274 crore loss on a legacy, fully provided equity exposure was grossed up in the presentation, and the Rs 159 crore treasury loss is the P&L line; the old exposure has no net P&L impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 NIM guided at 5.75% when Q4 adjusted is about 5.85%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said faster growth in wholesale and business banking is dilutive to margin, and 5.75% is among the highest in the banking system; Q4 was also boosted by day-count effects.

qa_highlights.question: What FY27 credit cost should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided 170-180 bps, including possible CGFMU recovery benefits; no quantum of CGFMU claims was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank need more capital and what about ECL transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more capital will be needed and a reset is expected; the CFO said the final ECL guidelines are still awaited and transition capital should be largely covered once they are issued.

qa_highlights.question: Is deposit competition intensifying, and what about SA/TD repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technology and branch strength will support deposits, and the CFO said residual TD repricing may affect Q1 FY27 but is largely done.

risks_watch: Deposit recovery: customer deposits grew only 1% QoQ in Q4, and management expects a return to normal growth in Q1 FY27; monitor monthly accretion and CASA ratio after the SA rate cut.
Fraud incident: Rs 646 crore claim settled and system fixes implemented; watch for further operational or reputational effects.
West Asia crisis: management has reviewed sector exposure and is being cautious on sectors facing demand, fuel and supply-chain stress; watch MSME slippages.
ECL transition: final RBI guidelines are awaited and may require additional capital.
Opex and cost-to-income: Q1 FY27 opex will run above the 13-14% guidance, and cost-to-income is about 73-74%.
Quality of earnings: Q4 benefited from a tax refund and day-count effects, and the treasury line was negative; watch the reported versus normalised gap.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the lending franchise and on deposit recovery, with management repeatedly stating that the deposit business will return to growth. Cautious and non-committal on specifics: it declined to give an ROA timeline or FY27 CGFMU recovery quantum, and framed the West Asia impact as limited so far.
key_quotes: Q1 FY '27 itself, you will see a strong growth in the bank.
the lending machine makes all the money, the deposit side is as of today is loss -making, but it will come to profitability.
Our bank is not earning on marginal costing. Our bank is earning on full costing, and that's a big difference.
We expect the profitability of the lending business to further improve next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on the lending franchise, deposit recovery and asset quality (GNPA 1.61%, credit cost down to 1.63%), but cautious on ROA timing, CGFMU recovery quantum and capital needs; analysts pressed on margin sustainability versus the Q4 run-rate and on ECL capital.
